Reasoning with Machines Lab · teaching demonstration

Beating John Snow's cholera map

Eight figures were briefed against the most famous data graphic ever made. Three judging lenses — accuracy, craft, and first glance — knocked them down to one over three rounds, and every surviving figure was rebuilt between rounds from the critiques that had just been levelled at it.

Echampion
Champion · Seed E · small multiples

The map convicts the pump. The clock cannot.

Beat D 3–0 · beat A 2–1 · beat F 2–1 in the final

Three matched small-multiple maps (all 578 deaths; the 359 nearest the Broad Street pump inside a computed straight-line catchment; the 219 nearest any of the other twelve) prove the spatial case with one dot per death and no hand-drawn boundary, while the daily attack/death curve below shows onsets had already fallen 92% and 92% of all attacks had begun before the handle came off on 8 September — so timing cannot carry the argument, only geography can.

Runner-up · Seed F · layered information

578 deaths. One pump.

Snow's case is spatial, not temporal, so this figure computes it rather than draws it: every death is assigned to its nearest pump by shortest path along Snow's own streets (map + catchment rail), and the missing denominator is answered with deaths per 100 m of street frontage by walking distance — steeply decaying for Broad Street, flat for all twelve other pumps — while the epidemic-curve strip is used to disqualify the handle-removal story rather than support it.

How F answered its semi-final

Regenerated from /Users/joshlawman/kb/teaching/reasoning-with-machines-lab/tournament/snow/entries/gen-sf-F.py (pure-Python SVG writer, evolved from gen-qf-F.py). Identity kept: same thesis, same four-panel A-B-C-D reading order, same serif-display/sans-label pairing, same computed catchment map.

ACCURACY (the fatal critique — panel B) — rebuilt from scratch

  • The smooth connected line over unequal ordinal bins is gone. Panel B is now a bar/step chart on TRUE, EQUAL bin widths: eight bands of exactly one map unit each (0-1 ... 7-8). The open-ended tail is no longer given a same-width slot; it is reported as a printed figure beside the axis ("beyond 8 units: 4 deaths / 276 units = 0.01").
  • The false "1 unit = 100 m, conventional" scale is removed everywhere. All distance is now stated in map units, since the argument never needed metres. The footnote derives the conversion honestly instead: Broad Street and Oxford Market pumps are 7.31 units apart and ~560 m apart on the modern street => roughly 75 m/unit, with the disclosure that independent georeferencings land between ~70 and 80 and that the often-quoted 100 m is too large. Map scale bar relabelled "2 map units, ~150 m by georeferencing".
  • Because the old rate was already deaths per (100 m / 100 m) = deaths per map unit, the plotted numbers are unchanged in value and merely correctly denominated: 18.83, 8.83, 9.81, 6.12, 3.64, 0.96, 0.35, 0.19.
  • The grey "range band" is replaced by all twelve rival pumps as individual step lines, drawn OVER the red bars with a white halo so each is checkable line by line.
  • Rhetoric pulled back to what the twelve lines actually show. Standfirst now claims only what I verified against the CSVs: every rival's maximum sits two or more units away from itself, and none tops 3.8 against Broad Street's 18.8 (max rival = 3.76, Oxford St #1, band 5-6). Removed "around no other pump does it climb at all" and the borderline "a fifth" ratio (3.76/18.83 = 0.1997).
  • The non-monotonic 1-2 dip is now called out in the annotation rather than smoothed away ("only 10.8 units of street fall in that band").

CRAFT

  • Gridlines are knocked out behind the panel-B annotation block and behind the new "other 12 pumps" legend.
  • The crammed terminal "0.2" is gone with the rebinning; small-bar labels get opaque paper haloes so the rival tangle doesn't strike through them.
  • The indecipherable tick-mark legend for a dashed representative is replaced by a plain leader line with a dot landing on the 3.8 ceiling.
  • Panel C: the twelve pale full-width zero-tracks are dropped entirely; bars sit on a real zero baseline plus a 0/100/200/300/374 count axis, zero rows get a tick and "0", and the orphaned floating baseline label is gone. The 374 label moved inside the bar so it no longer overflows the margin.
  • Footnote lifted to AA contrast (MUTE #6E675C -> #5E594F, FAINT -> #8C8578, uniform tone, 8.7 px), paper stock lightened to #FDFCF8.

Stolen from the defeated opponent: their praised discipline of printing the raw numerator/denominator under the claim (panel B now prints the tail's 4/276, panel C prints every count against a real axis) and their linear, lay-parseable comparison instead of anything log-scaled. Avoided their sinking flaw by keeping labels out of the death cluster.

Additional fix found by looking: the in-map key was occluding the Vigo St pump (and, when moved, Castle St E). Both in-map boxes were deleted and the key + scale bar now sit in the empty band below the map frame, so nothing on the cartography is covered at all. Canvas grew to 1360x1222 to accommodate.

Verified by rendering with rsvg-convert at 1900-2100 px and reading the full figure plus crops of panels A, B and C; all overlaps found in those passes were fixed and re-checked. File is valid XML, self-contained, no external references.

Champion's revision log

What E changed after the semi-final

Kept the identity (A/B/C matched nearest-pump small multiples + D epidemic strip + computed Voronoi catchment) and evolved it.

ACCURACY critiques acted on

  • Crop widened to X 8.12–19.18, Y 4.82–18.78 so ALL 13 pumps and all 578 deaths sit inside every frame, enforced by two new assertions (`assert all(X0 < p[2] < X1 ...)`) — the legend's "the other 12 pumps — all inside frame" is now literally true instead of hiding 5.
  • Ledger now lists all 13 pumps ranked, zeros included (Oxford Market, 0), with a note that the emptiness is evidence so it is listed, not hidden. A zero count draws no bar at all rather than a misleading 1px stub.
  • Every prose number is derived: 219 (n_o), 64 (top rival, looked up by rank), "18% of Broad Street's 359" replaces the hardcoded "under a fifth", rival name So Soho pulled from the CSV, zero-pump count and names computed, street-vertex count computed. Nothing about the data is typed by hand.
  • Stole the defeated opponent's disclosure discipline: footer now states panel D is Snow's Table 1 (571 attacks, 616 deaths, plus 45 attacks of unstated date, excluded) and that the series counts more deaths than the 578 mapped addresses and cannot be linked case by case.

CRAFT critiques acted on

  • "ENTRY E · REVISED" production tag deleted.
  • Ledger bars darkened two steps (#a49b8f) so 64 / 61 / 27 / 24 / 16 read as an encoding on cream; Broad Street stays red.
  • Panel D's five-line paragraph pulled out of the plot area into a right-hand side caption; the plot region now carries only bars, the death line, the dashed 8 Sept rule and the peak leader.
  • Scale bar moved off the map into the left-hand key block, clear of all map ink; added a north arrow in panel B.
  • Red is now reserved strictly for Broad Street data-ink: panel A's dots are dark ink, not red (stolen from the opponent's colour-discipline critique). Deaths line recoloured to a deeper red so it doesn't compete with the pale attack bars.

FIRST-GLANCE critiques acted on

  • Equal-thirds grid broken: panel B is the hero at double width (546 × 689), A and C are flanking thumbnails; the space freed under A holds the key/scale, under C the 13-pump ledger.

Layout/typography fixes found by looking at the render: added a word-wrap helper so the take-away and footer no longer run off the page, an `assert fy + 20 < H` canvas-overflow guard, moved the peak label left of the peak to stop it colliding with "8 Sept: the handle comes off", and raised the panel-D caption so it clears the take-away rule.

Round one

Quarter-final 1 — A v H

The pump, not the air · Soho, London, 1854 against The Range of a Pump

A advances, 2 – 1 — The Range of a Pump is out.

The StatisticianArithmetic integrity, reproducibility, honest denominators
A9.2vote

Strongest quality: the headline analysis is real and exactly reproducible — I re-ran shortest-path catchments over Snow's street graph myself and got A's bar chart to the death (374/71/56/26/22/14/11/2/1/1), every one of the 578 dots is plotted from the data to within 0.07 px, all dots are in frame, and the red/grey classification has zero mismatches against an independent computation; the "what this figure cannot show" footer is model data honesty. Worst flaw: the presentation quietly flatters its own punchline — "only 8% of mapped street length" is 8.6% by my replication (and 9.3 vs my 9.16 deaths/100 m), red Broad-St dots are drawn 28% larger in area than grey dots (r=3.4 vs 3.0) with grey at low contrast, and the 24-px tan catchment buffer (~45 m half-width) makes an 8.6%-of-street-length catchment read as a large filled district. Fix: equalize dot sizes (differ by hue only), state 8.6% or show the split method that yields 8%, and thin the catchment buffer to the street width so the area impression matches the length statistic.

H8.6

Strongest quality: numerically immaculate — every death is plotted within 0.07 px of the data, and every annotation I checked is exact (median 217 m / 422 m, all 13 panel-C medians within rounding, 59.5%≈60% within 250 m, exactly 15 deaths beyond 500 m, exactly 36 occupied 10° sectors, peak 127), with an honesty note that even flags the straight-line-vs-walking issue. Worst flaw: it chose the analytically weaker metric and buries the correction — straight-line distance misassigns deaths near catchment boundaries (Euclidean nearest-pump gives Broad St 359 vs the true walking 374), the bold headline "Half of all deaths fell within 217 m" will be read as walking proximity by anyone who skips the footnote, and the petal histogram has no count scale at all, so "deaths per 10° bearing" is unreadable as magnitude — only as occupancy. Fix: either compute walking distance along Snow's streets (it's the argument Snow actually made) or put "straight-line" in the headline itself, and give the petals a labeled count scale or two reference ticks.

The Art EditorTypography, colour discipline, collisions, house style
A6.5

Strongest quality: genuinely disciplined editorial grid — serif display heads over sans body, a two-hue palette (Broad-St red vs. neutral grey) held rigorously across map, legend and bars, and a well-ordered right rail with numbered panels and an honest footer. Worst flaw: the tan walking-catchment is rendered as fat round-capped strokes that merge into a lumpy, scalloped amoeba with visible nubs and overlap seams at every street end — it reads as highlighter smear, not cartography — and the halo-boxed "BROAD STREET PUMP" label (with cramped tracking between STREET and PUMP) sits directly on top of the death dots, occluding the very data the figure argues from. Secondary sins: panel 3 is a crude two-bar chart whose 9.3 bar is drawn at nearly the same length as panel 2's 374 bar directly above it, inviting a false visual equation; pump-label placement on the map is inconsistent (above, below, left of the symbol, case by case). Concrete fix: rebuild the catchment as a single dissolved polygon with a flat fill and no per-segment caps, and move the pump label off the dot cluster with a leader line.

H8vote

Strongest quality: the polar composition is a confident, original piece of craft — concentric distance rings, a restrained warm palette in one red-orange family, an elegant 10°-bearing petal ring, and exemplary direct annotation in panel B (the 60%/250 m callout with leader, "Briddle St, next-best pump" labelled in situ) that a Nature art editor would applaud. Worst flaw: text-measure discipline collapses outside the panels — the dek, the map caption block, and the two-line honesty note all run edge-to-edge at roughly 130+ characters per line, far past comfortable measure, and the panel lettering starts at B with the hero map never labelled A, leaving the sequence visibly broken; diamond-pump labels also anchor inconsistently (text left of So Soho, right of Briddle St, nearly touching the glyph). Concrete fix: cap all running text at ~75 characters (split the honesty note into a two-column footer), label the map "A." beside its caption, and standardize pump-label offsets.

The Lay ReaderWhat the figure says in eight seconds
A8.5vote

Strongest quality: the title is the thesis — "The pump, not the air" plus the red 374/578 banner means the claim is received before the map is even parsed, and the numbered 1-4 rail forces reading order. Worst flaw at a glance: the map's own evidence is muddier than the headline — the grey "other-pump" deaths are near-invisible at arm's length, so the red cluster looks like ALL the deaths rather than a contrast, and the tiny bullseye pump glyph is carried entirely by its text label; the amorphous beige catchment blob reads as a coffee stain until panel 1 explains it. Fix: triple the pump marker's size and give the catchment a crisp darker outline, so the geometry (red inside, grey outside, pump at center) argues by itself even if every word were deleted.

H7

Strongest quality: "Half of all deaths fell within 217 m" is the crispest single-number claim of either entry, and panel B's lone red curve sprinting ahead of twelve grey ones is a genuinely great glance-legible chart. Worst flaw: the hero polar plot self-sabotages under first-glance conditions — centering the frame on Broad Street guarantees dots surround the center, so a smart reader's instant reaction is "circular reasoning," and the rebuttal (217 vs 422 m, all 36 bearings occupied) is buried in the right rail and a bottom caption; meanwhile the headline "THE RANGE OF A PUMP" names a topic, not a verdict. Fix: put the claim in the title ("Deaths ringed one pump — Broad Street") and add two thumbnail polar small-multiples centered on Briddle St and Crown Chapel next to the hero, so the glance itself shows the disc collapses when you center anywhere else.

Round one

Quarter-final 2 — D v E

The pump on Broad Street against The map convicts the pump. The clock cannot.

E advances, 3 – 0 — The pump on Broad Street is out.

The StatisticianArithmetic integrity, reproducibility, honest denominators
D6.5

Strongest quality: near-forensic fidelity everywhere else — all 578 deaths plotted at 0.05px accuracy, all 13 pumps from coordinates, a nearest-pump table that is exactly right (359/64/61/27/24/16/27), and honest 'not in the data' flags. Worst flaw: the timeline panel is a chart lie — the legend promises a 'new attacks' line that is never drawn, the bars are actually the DEATHS series (peak 127, 2 Sep) while the annotation 'peak: 143 new attacks, 1 Sept' floats at 143-height over them, and the prose claim that attacks collapsed 'to single figures before the handle came off' is false (28 on 7 Sep, 12 on 8 Sep; single digits only from 10 Sep). Fix: draw the attacks line you promised (both series, like Snow's Table 1), move the 143 callout onto that line at 1 Sep, and rewrite the sentence to what the data supports — 'attacks had fallen 92% from the peak before the handle came off.'

E8vote

Strongest quality: the encoding IS the argument — all three panels replot the identical 578 deaths sub-pixel from data, the B/C highlight split is exactly the Euclidean nearest-pump partition (359/219), the timeline carries both series correctly (attacks 143 / deaths 127), and the footnotes disclose Euclidean-vs-walking, counts-not-rates, and unlinkable series. Worst flaw: '62% fall inside the catchment, half of them within 217 m' misattaches a real number — 217 m is the median over ALL 578 deaths; the median for the 359 in-catchment deaths is ~158 m — and 'after the handle: 8% of attacks, 19% of deaths' mixes cutoff conventions (strictly-after is 7.0%/18.8%, inclusive is 8.9%/23.7%). Fix: recompute the median on the subset the sentence actually refers to (or say 'half of all 578'), pick one cutoff convention for the post-handle shares and state it, and note the 1 unit = 100 m scale assumption behind every metre figure.

The Art EditorTypography, colour discipline, collisions, house style
D7

Strongest quality: a confident editorial typographic system — the numbered read-order strip, letterspaced sans kickers against Georgia display, and the black closing band are genuinely distinctive. Worst flaw: unresolved label collisions at final size — the "peak: 143 new attacks, 1 Sept" text runs straight through the 8-Sept vertical rule, "Dean St" crashes into the brewery callout (with another label ghosting through the translucent box), "Oxford St #1" is clipped by the map border, and the corner legend sits on live death dots. Concrete fix: run a collision pass — move the peak label left of the rule, make callout boxes fully opaque with a 1px keyline, pull "Dean St" and its square inside the frame, and put the legend/scale on an opaque card; also consider cutting the map callouts from five to three, since the boxes currently occlude the very cluster the piece is about.

E8.2vote

Strongest quality: journal-grade structure — three identically framed small multiples with A–D panel letters, one disciplined red with ghost-beige/dark-grey de-emphasis (panel C's inversion is the best colour decision in the tournament), and a proper sources-and-method footnote. Worst flaw: text set over chart furniture without knockouts — the 100-cases gridline strikes through "and 92% of all attacks in the outbreak had already begun.", the red leader clips the words "the peak", and "Broad Street pump" / "approx. 200 m" sit on death dots. Concrete fix: add white halo or gridline-break behind every annotation, shorten the peak leader so it lands beside not through the text, and remove the empty double-ruled bracket box under "after the handle came off" — the shaded region already carries that message; one border is enough.

The Lay ReaderWhat the figure says in eight seconds
D6.5

Strongest quality: the headline states the claim outright ("The pump on Broad Street") and the pump marker has genuine hierarchy — filled blue disc with halo against hollow squares — so a non-epidemiologist knows which pump is on trial. Worst flaw: the argument is asserted in prose but never delivered in ink. Five opaque callout boxes are laid ON TOP of the map and occlude roughly half of it, chopping the death cluster into disconnected fragments so the eye never resolves the one shape the whole figure exists to show; and the presence of a literal "READ IN ORDER ①②③④⑤" strip is self-indicting evidence that order is NOT forced — ④ floats inside the map's top-right while ⑤ sits across the gutter in a different column, sending the eye on a diagonal jump within the first three seconds. Concrete fix: evict every callout box from the map rectangle into a margin rail or below-map row and let the dot cluster occupy the full 796x742 frame uninterrupted; if annotations must touch the map, reduce them to numbered pins with leader lines and put the text outside. Second fix: the twelve rival pumps are drawn so faintly they never register, so the "nearest pump" comparison lives only in the bar chart — give each rival pump a visible catchment or at minimum a marker weight that survives the squint test.

E7.5vote

Strongest quality: at 25% zoom the pink catchment hull in panel B is the single thing that pops off the page, and it happens to BE the argument — "the dead fall inside this one pump's zone" reads without a caption and without any epidemiology; the A/B/C/D lettering plus row structure forces reading order by layout alone, needing no instruction strip. Worst flaw: the hull is a convex boundary drawn over a non-convex nearest-pump catchment, so on close inspection red member dots sit visibly OUTSIDE the dashed line along its northeast edge while gray non-member dots sit inside it — a skeptical reader hits that contradiction by second three and starts doubting the 62% the panel just claimed. Concrete fix: replace the convex hull with the actual Voronoi cell boundary for the Broad Street pump (or an alpha-shape tight to the member points) so that every red dot is inside the line and every gray dot outside — the claim then verifies itself visually. Second issue: the headline is a two-clause rhetorical construction whose second half ("The clock cannot") means nothing until panel D is read, and panel D consumes roughly 30% of the ink arguing the negative claim; consider shrinking D to a strip and letting the title lead with the positive finding.

Round one

Quarter-final 3 — B v G

The pump, not the air — nearest-pump allocation and distance decay, Soho 1854 against A pump, not a neighbourhood: street-network attribution of the 1854 Broad Street cholera deaths

G advances, 2 – 1 — The pump, not the air — nearest-pump allocation and distance decay, Soho 1854 is out.

The StatisticianArithmetic integrity, reproducibility, honest denominators
B6.5

Arithmetically the most accurate entry I could verify: I rebuilt the graph myself (1,241 points → 558 nodes, 713 edges, as it states) and got Broad St 375 by edge-projection and exactly 359 by Euclidean Voronoi — its 376/202 and its 359 robustness claim reproduce, its per-pump bars match mine within 1–2, and 376+202=578 with 378 filled and 206 open circles actually on the page. But it contains a flat factual error on its own timing panel: "peak 143 attacks, 31 Aug" — 143 attacks fell on 1 September (31 Aug had 56), and the error tilts the argument by pushing the peak a day further from the 8 Sept handle removal; the subtitle likewise dates the 578 to "31 August – 30 September" while its own axis and the data start 19 August. Worse for the lens, the blurred pink blob is legended as "ground closer to Broad St on foot" — a 1-D street partition rendered as a soft 2-D territory, and the rendered figure visibly contradicts it (red Broad-nearest dots sit outside the blob at top-left and far right, open other-pump dots sit inside it); the gaussian edge also reads as a death-density heat map, a quantity never computed. Panel B compounds this with a dashed "raw death count (rescaled)" series sharing the per-100 m axis with no second scale, no values and no stated factor, so its height and its apparent crossing of the bars are meaningless, and the red/grey bar recolouring implies a threshold at 108 m that is not in the data. Concrete fix: correct the date to 1 Sept, replace the blur with the hard Voronoi boundary drawn along the streets it was actually computed on, and either give the raw-count line its own labelled right axis or delete it.

G7.5vote

Its per-band "deaths 31/2 … metres of street 143/1555" strip is the single most honest device in either entry — every plotted point can be recomputed by the reader, and I confirmed 17× (13.0 vs 0.75 per 100 m), 20-fold (0.155 vs 0.0074 per m), 67%/9%, the 31-on-143-m takeaway, and the correct 127-death peak on 2 Sept; the map overlay stays on the street centre-lines, which is what the method actually partitions, and the fragile 250–300 m band (44 deaths on 121 m) is flagged in place plus re-run without it. Its n=386 is ~11 too generous to Broad Street relative to edge projection (I get 375–376), though it reproduces exactly under the nearest-node snapping it discloses (I get 387) — the disclosure saves it, but it reports a metric robustness check and never the snapping sensitivity that actually moves its headline. The real distortions are in panel b: a pink area filled from the red step curve down to the baseline on a log axis, where area encodes nothing and simply dramatises the gap, and two "0 deaths" points drawn at a fabricated position below 0.1 where zero cannot exist; the top decade is unlabelled, so the curve's ~36 per 100 m peak is unreadable, and the 200 m isochrone ticks render as pink smears barely distinguishable from the zone shading. Concrete fix: kill the log-axis area fill and the off-scale zeros (state "0 deaths on 1,784 m" in the table instead), label the top decade, and add one line reporting Broad's count under edge projection so readers see 386 is method-dependent.

The Art EditorTypography, colour discipline, collisions, house style
B7

B ("The pump, not the air") has the better typographic system of the two — a serif display face against a sans text face, real eyebrow/deck/subdeck hierarchy, a well-set kicker bar, and disciplined footnote rules — but it is a newspaper graphic, not a journal figure, and its worst craft flaw is the airbrushed pink catchment: a Gaussian-blurred glow blob with no defined boundary, sitting under blurred red street strokes. A Nature art editor rejects soft-glow raster effects on sight (they also degrade in CMYK and at 89 mm column width), and here the blur destroys the very edge the figure claims to draw. Colour discipline then breaks twice more: panel B splits the same decay series into red bars and grey bars at an arbitrary 160 m cut, so hue encodes nothing; and panel C immediately reuses that identical red/grey pair to mean deaths vs attacks, so red carries two incompatible meanings within 200 px. Add the decorative red "straight-line rings, for scale" circles and radial spokes that cross the data (their caption text collides with a street and with the "215 m" label), the counts duplicated in both map labels and panel A, "peak 143 attacks, 31 Aug" struck through by its own bars, an unlabelled second scale for the dashed "raw death count (rescaled)" line, and roughly the bottom third of the map frame left as dead space while the right column is crammed. Concrete fix: delete the blur entirely — render the catchment as a flat 8–10% tint with a crisp 0.5 pt edge — and make red mean exactly one thing per figure (Broad Street), recolouring panel B's bars a single hue with the gradient carried by height alone.

G7.8vote

G is the only one of the two a Nature art editor could send to press largely as-is: bold lowercase a/b panel letters, a proper "Figure 1 |" caption with legend, a single sans family at consistent weights, one red plus neutral greys, an honest log axis with the deaths/metres denominators tabulated under the band ticks, scale bar, and a stated north — restraint carried the whole way through. Its worst craft flaw is collision and contrast in panel a: the daily-deaths inset is an unframed white knockout that slices the street network on a hard rectangular edge and amputates the left half of the Vigo St pump square, while the pump glyphs elsewhere are drawn in the same light grey value as the streets and effectively vanish; the salmon "200 m isochrone ticks" read as smeared, unresolvable pink smudges beneath the dot cloud rather than as a boundary, and the dense red dots merge into solid mass with no transparency or size reduction. Secondary sins: the title runs the full 1300 px measure in one line, the right column leaves a large void below the takeaway box while panel a is crowded, and the final band spikes upward on a log axis (with "0 deaths" points floated below the axis with no break marker), visually contradicting the decay story the figure is selling. Concrete fix: give the inset a hairline keyline and reposition it clear of the Vigo St pump, then darken pump squares to near-black and replace the pink isochrone ticks with a single continuous thin isochrone line.

The Lay ReaderWhat the figure says in eight seconds
B8vote

Strongest: the eight-second takeaway is unmissable and correct — "The pump, not the air," a red 376-of-578 banner, and a single red glow-blob on the map whose centre is a ringed, labelled BROAD ST PUMP. The z-path (title, banner, map, then A/B/C stack) is genuinely forced, and the red-vs-hollow-blue dot encoding needs no epidemiology to decode; even at 500px thumbnail the argument survives. Worst flaw: the pink kernel-density halo is the loudest mark on the page and it is not data — it smears 578 precise addresses into an airbrushed smudge, which is exactly the miasma-shaped blob the title claims to refute, and it swallows the street network beneath it. Concrete fix: drop the glow to a flat 10%-alpha catchment polygon clipped to the street graph (or kill it and let the red dots do the work), and delete the faint "215 m" straight-line dotted rings — a Euclidean scale ring inside a walking-distance figure is a mixed metaphor that costs a reader two seconds of confusion for no gain. Secondary: the per-pump counts printed on the map ("Crown Chapel 73") duplicate panel A exactly; drop them from the map and let A own the ranking.

G6.5

Strongest: panel b is the better piece of analysis on the page — a log-scale mortality-per-100-m step comparison of the Broad zone against the twelve pooled pumps, with the deaths/metres tallies laid under the axis, is a genuinely harder and more honest claim than a raw count. Worst flaw: nothing on the page is sized like a headline. The title is a 28px sentence with a colon and the word "attribution" in it; the actual number (67% of deaths on 9% of street length) is buried in body-size text inside a TAKEAWAY box in the bottom-right dead zone, which is the last place any eye lands. Afaithful modernizationQuarter-final 1 · advanced v H

The pump, not the air · Soho, London, 1854

Snow's map, re-encoded: one dot per death instead of tally bars, and the walking-distance catchment recomputed by Dijkstra over his own street lines — showing 65% of deaths crowded into 8% of the street network around the Broad Street pump, with the missing population denominator declared rather than implied.

Bdata-forwardQuarter-final 3 · eliminated v G

The pump, not the air — nearest-pump allocation and distance decay, Soho 1854

It converts Snow's map into a statistical allocation: multi-source Dijkstra over the reconstructed street graph assigns each of the 578 deaths to the pump nearest on foot (Broad St 376, 65%, 1.9x all twelve others; Euclidean Voronoi agrees within 17), and a street-length-denominated distance-decay panel shows deaths per 100 m of street falling monotonically 27 to 0.1 with walking distance — proving the gradient is not an artefact of there simply being more Soho further out.

One pump.

Reduce Snow's map to two marks — a dot per death, tone-coded by which of the 13 pumps is nearest, and the exact nearest-pump boundary around Broad Street — so the argument reads as one sentence (62% of the dead inside 13% of the ground), with a single ranked count-by-pump bar replacing the uncomparable address tallies and explicit notes that the boundary is straight-line, the curve was already falling before the handle came off, and no denominator exists.

DeditorialQuarter-final 2 · eliminated v E

The pump on Broad Street

A forced-order annotated map — five numbered stops from the dot cluster to the pump, to the groups that drank other water (brewery, workhouse), to the Hampstead widow killed by carted Broad Street water, to the handle's removal — replaces Snow's uncomparable tally bars with plain dots plus straight-line distance rings and a nearest-pump count, and states in the figure itself that there is no denominator, that the walking-distance boundary was drawn afterwards, and that the epidemic was already falling when the handle came off.

Esmall multiplesQuarter-final 2 · advanced v D

The map convicts the pump. The clock cannot.

Three matched small-multiple maps (all 578 deaths; the 359 nearest the Broad Street pump inside a computed straight-line catchment; the 219 nearest any of the other twelve) prove the spatial case with one dot per death and no hand-drawn boundary, while the daily attack/death curve below shows onsets had already fallen 92% and 92% of all attacks had begun before the handle came off on 8 September — so timing cannot carry the argument, only geography can.

Flayered informationQuarter-final 4 · advanced v C

578 deaths. One pump.

Snow's case is spatial, not temporal, so this figure computes it rather than draws it: every death is assigned to its nearest pump by shortest path along Snow's own streets (map + catchment rail), and the missing denominator is answered with deaths per 100 m of street frontage by walking distance — steeply decaying for Broad Street, flat for all twelve other pumps — while the epidemic-curve strip is used to disqualify the handle-removal story rather than support it.

A pump, not a neighbourhood: street-network attribution of the 1854 Broad Street cholera deaths

It argues that the Broad Street excess is an attribute of one pump rather than of a district, by attributing every death to its shortest-walk pump over Snow's own street graph (panel a) and then giving the map the denominator it never had — deaths per 100 m of street frontage by walking distance, Broad zone versus the other twelve pooled, with per-band counts and metres printed (panel b) — yielding a 20-fold difference per metre with its limitations and two robustness variants stated in the caption.

HwildcardQuarter-final 1 · eliminated v A

The Range of a Pump

Re-projecting Snow's 578 deaths into polar coordinates centred on the Broad Street pump turns the map into a measurement: half of all deaths lie within 217 m of that pump (next-best pump: 422 m), the deaths occupy all 36 compass sectors so it is a disc rather than a corridor, and a cumulative distance-decay curve per pump lets the reader compare all thirteen candidates on one honest, denominator-free statistic — where the deaths already were.

Beating John Snow's cholera map. Reasoning with Machines Lab teaching demonstration. Source data: Snow's 1854 Broad Street death addresses (578 mapped), thirteen pump coordinates, and Snow's Table 1 daily attacks and deaths.
